text:
tara (PM): Quick sync — 1.2 private launch window is tentatively Oct 18. Need a hard decision on network mode defaults. Two options on the table: preserve-customer-egress-ip (BGP/peering) or nat-relay fallback. Field says a few anchor customers won't accept relay. Thoughts?

mike (Eng): short take: relay = fastest path (1 sprint), preserve-ip = more infra + operator work (~4 sprints). preserve needs operator shim, operator lifecycle hooks, and QA for BGP flaps. relay requires NAT relay service + egress ACL docs.

olivia (Field): Acme & FinCorp explicitly require IP preservation in contracts. If we ship relay-only, we'll lose both initial pilots. Can we ship relay for GA but offer preserve as opt-in early-access?

junaid (NetOps): preserve-ip constraints: static egress IP allocation, BGP peering, IPAM mapping per-tenant. Acceptance criteria we need from product: expected tenant scale, allowed ASNs, and failover policy. Also need a runbook for peering rotate.

sam (SRE): ops concerns: preserve-ip means customer routing becomes part of our blast radius if misconfigured. Must have a safe rollback toggle in the operator and a canary plan. Also add health probes: egress-ip-heartbeat and bgp-adj-state. Ticketed as INFOPS-721.

mike (Eng): optional installer flag prototype below for preserve mode:
```
redwood-installer --mode preserve-ip \n  --bgp-asn 65010 \n  --egress-ips 203.0.113.10-203.0.113.20 \n  --enable-operator-shim=true
```
Notes: operator-shim will own BGP sessions and AS-path tagging. We'll need to version the shim separately from main runtime.

olivia (Field): if we do opt-in EA for preserve-ip, customers expect clear SLAs and a 'network-ready' checklist for them. Also they want ability to test without full production traffic. Can we provide a staging handoff template? :eyes: 

junaid (NetOps): agree. Handoff template should include: expected eBGP peer IPs, allowed prefixes, community tagging, and a contact escalation matrix. NetOps can pre-authorize peers if template filled.

tara (PM): proposal: ship relay as default for GA (low effort), and run a prioritized EA cohort for preserve-ip. EA acceptance gates: operator shim GA (integration tests pass), runbook complete, 2 pilot customers validated for 72h with zero egress drift. If pilots pass, we flip the button for paid opt-in.

sam (SRE): add metric gating: bgp-adj-stability >= 99.95% over 24h, egress-ip-consistency <= 1 mismatch per 10k flows. Also require automated rollback on route flaps > 5 in 10m.

mike (Eng): engineering ask: need 8 dev-weeks for operator shim PoC, plus 2 QA sprints. If we run EA in parallel, we can deliver opt-in in 6-8 weeks. Relay GA path remains 2 weeks.

olivia (Field): prioritization note: committing to EA for preserve-ip unlocks two enterprise deals. If we skip EA we push those deals by a quarter. Recommend PM prioritize shim work. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tara (PM): decision for today: prioritize relay for GA to hit Oct 18. Start operator-shim spike immediately and schedule EA slots for Nov pilots. Action items: mike scope shim PoC (ENG-1298), junaid draft handoff template (NETOPS-452), sam define probes & automated rollback playbook (SRE-721). Olivia, list pilot customer contacts and timeline.

deploy-bot: CI update — feature/operator-shim spike branch created. Unit tests: pass. E2E: queued.

mike (Eng): noted on ENG-1298, will add a small config-driven toggle to the runtime so we can flip preserve-ip at runtime without restart. That will help rollback.

olivia (Field): adding pilot contacts: acme-netops@acme.io, ops@fincorp.com. Target pilot window Nov 2–9. I'll set expectations that it's opt-in and may have limited telemetry initially.

junaid (NetOps): draft handoff posted to the docs repo: /docs/onprem/preserve-ip-handoff.md — includes eBGP checklist and sample ASNs. Will link once PR is up.

sam (SRE): I'll write the probe definitions and a simple k8s job that verifies egress ip mapping every 5m. If mismatch count > 3 in 30m, trigger operator toggle.

tara (PM): thanks team. I'll update the roadmap board: GA = relay default (Oct 18), EA preserve-ip (Nov pilots), GA opt-in availability (Dec, contingent). We'll revisit SLA language after pilots.

mike (Eng): one more tech callout: preserve-ip across multi-zone clusters needs symmetric return-path handling. We'll prototype on single AZ first and note multi-AZ as follow-up.

olivia (Field): great — will communicate to pilot customers and start pre-req checklist. :thumbsup:
